YOUR LENS: failure, recovery and concurrency semantics. Walk every effect (registry publish, tag create+push, GitHub release draft/upload/publish, release-PR commit) and ask: what if the process dies right before / right after / during it; what if the registry shows the version late, shows a DIFFERENT artifact, rate-limits, or returns 5xx; what if two runs overlap (CI re-run, two merges, local + CI); what if HEAD moves between plan and execute; what if a tag exists remotely but not locally or points elsewhere; what if the registry accepts the publish but the response is lost (non-idempotent effect with unknown outcome); partial multi-package/multi-registry releases and how a rerun adopts them (ADR 3); the E320 version-commit logic (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/version_commit.rs) and the confirmation window / ConfirmationWave (release_execution.rs); fixed-group and dual-ecosystem packages; Python multi-file uploads; npm dist-tag outcomes; wall-clock and timeout handling; receipts. # RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Memory Index

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).
- [Prove With the Real Tool](feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md) — Fake-tool tests and clean compiles hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; reproduce auth/release/registry paths with the real tool, test the failing case first, state what is unproven.
- [Callisto Self-Release Incident — Durable Memory](project_release_self_hosting_incident_2026-09.md) — Claude invented and later misattributed the release approval gate, misunderstood rerun semantics, and repeatedly declared fixes before publication; records non-negotiable policy, verified failures, corrective architecture, and required incident protocol.
- [Hardcoded Values — Proactive Search Required](feedback_hardcoded_values.md) — User repeatedly frustrated by missed hardcoded values; always include a dedicated pass in any audit or fix session.
- [Track 0: gix WASI spike — NO-GO verdict](project_track0_wasi_verdict.md) — mmap ENOSYS in WASI blocks all gix object reads; callisto-moon exec-seam must use warpgate_pdk::exec_command.
- [Publish Pipeline Audit — 38 bugs, fix ordering, semantic coupling map](project_publish_pipeline_audit.md) — Full adversarial audit complete; 5 P0s, 11 P1s, 15+ P2s; three root patterns; phased fix sequence with dependency order.
- [Parallel Fixing Anti-Pattern](feedback_parallel_fixing.md) — Parallel agents for fixes fail on semantically coupled systems even across different files; use parallel for investigation only.
- [Validate Each Fix Individually](feedback_validate_each_fix.md) — Run targeted tests after every individual fix; do not batch changes and rely solely on final CI run.
- Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/architecture/ (moved from .claude/semantic-model on 2026-09-25) — read before implementation work.
- [Active Work](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) — Tracks B, E, F (resolve_package_config), G (callisto matrix) all shipped and passing just ci. Pipeline: canon→vector→lambda.
- [Canon Pipeline Scope](feedback_canon_pipeline_scope.md) — Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose.
- [Workspace Audit 2026-08](project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md) — CLOSED: 8-dimension audit, all critical/high + all 31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed as of 2026-08-27.
- [Found Code Needs Same Rigor](feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md) — Committing pre-existing uncommitted code after only "compiles + existing tests pass" missed a zero-test-coverage regression; found/inherited code needs the same TDD/adversarial rigor as freshly-written code.
- [Manifest Persist Track](project_manifest_persist_track.md) — Both Spec A (mutate/persist split) and Spec B (write-batching) shipped; the apply_version_plan redundant-open/persist audit finding is fully closed.
- [Reviewer Must Actually Run Checks](feedback_reviewer_must_actually_run_checks.md) — lambda-reviewer falsely reported clippy clean once; always instruct review agents to run commands for real, not infer results.
- [Iterate Reviews in Foreground](feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground.md) — Background agent notifications were unreliable across a multi-round spec/plan review loop; user called it out twice — run tight revise-review cycles in the foreground.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

3. **Verify before reporting**: Try to disprove the finding first (check for a guard you may have missed). Give a concrete failing scenario (specific input, state, or flag). Mark `CONFIRMED` (path fully traced) or `PLAUSIBLE` (strong signal, not fully traced).

A finding that names only the first instance you tripped over, when siblings exist, is an incomplete finding.

---

# Universal Rust Bug-Hunter Skill

## Goal

Find real bugs before they ship in any Rust repository (monorepos, CLI engines, libraries, polyglot WASM plugins): silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, data corruption, ordering staleness, crash-safety violations, and edge cases that break production.

This skill is **Rigid**: follow it exactly across any Rust workspace.

## The Law

> NO FINDING MARKED `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT AN END-TO-END TRACE. NO FIX MARKED DONE WITHOUT A TEST THAT FAILED BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER, RUN IN THIS SESSION.

## Core Rules

- **Verify by Tracing**: Don't trust a comment, docstring, passing test, or a prior audit's "FIXED" label. Trace the code execution path yourself.
- **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: When executing multi-agent bug hunts, DO NOT partition subagents by directory or crate names. ALWAYS partition subagents by **Hazard Taxonomy** or **Code Smell Sweep** across the entire workspace.
- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.
- **Read-Only Investigation**: Investigate and report findings first. Do not mutate files unless explicitly requested to apply fixes.

---

## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies

1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.

---

## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps

1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.

---

## 7 Shared Trait Centralization Framework

When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.

---

## Hazard-Taxonomy Multi-Agent Dispatch Matrix

| Agent Role | Scope | Objective |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`bug-hunter-scanner-rust`** | Taxonomies 1 & 4 | Scan workspace for unused CLI flags, discarded parameters, and silent `unwrap_or` defaults. |
| **`bug-hunter-adversary-rust`** | Taxonomies 2 & 3 | Trace execution paths end-to-end, disprove candidate signals, and check graph solver fixpoints and spec drift. |
| **`bug-hunter-remediator-rust`** | Taxonomies 5 & 6 | Audit boundary inputs, atomic write `.flush()`/`.sync_all()`, write failing regression tests (red), apply fixes. |
| **`bug-hunter-architect-rust`** | Smells 1-6 & Trait Centralization | Analyze recurring defect patterns, cluster code smells, and design lean Rust traits with formal contracts. |
| **`bug-hunter-mutator-rust`** | Mutation Testing & Coverage | Run `cargo-mutants`, find survived mutant branches, and write boundary unit tests ensuring assertions fail when code is mutated. |

---

## Evaluation Output Standard

Report each confirmed finding in this standard technical format:

```markdown
### [Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low] <Brief Vulnerability Title>

- **Status**: CONFIRMED (execution path fully traced, file:line cited) | PLAUSIBLE (strong signal, not fully traced)
- **Location**: `path/to/file.rs:L123-L135`

- **Root Cause**: Concise explanation of the flaw in the current implementation logic.
- **Failing Scenario**: Concrete payload, CLI command, or input state that triggers the defect.
- **Verification Strategy**: A test that fails on current code and passes once fixed.
```

10	You audit any target Rust codebase for latent bugs: silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, ordering/staleness bugs, crash-safety violations, and security/edge-case gaps using Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies.
11	
12	## Operational Directives
13	
14	0. **Read-only**: Investigate and report; do not edit files or run mutating commands unless the task explicitly asks for a fix. Read `../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` (if present) — skip re-reporting anything already logged as `CONFIRMED`. This ledger lives outside the repo, deliberately — it names unfixed defects and must never be committed here (this repo is public).
15	1. **Trace end-to-end**: Don't stop at interface boundaries — follow data from CLI/API inputs through domain models, graph algorithms, manifest editors, down to disk I/O.
16	2. **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: Execute audits focused on specific Hazard Categories (1. Discarded Parameters, 2. Fixpoint Staleness, 3. Spec Drift, 4. Silent Fallbacks, 5. Boundary Edge Cases, 6. Crash-Safety & Subprocesses) across the entire target workspace.
17	3. **Verify before reporting**: Try to disprove the finding first (check for a guard you may have missed). Give a concrete failing scenario (specific input, state, or flag). Mark `CONFIRMED` (path fully traced) or `PLAUSIBLE` (strong signal, not fully traced).
18	4. **Structured Reporting**: Use the format in `../skills/bug-hunter/SKILL.md` — Status, Location (`file:line`), Classification, Root Cause, Failing Scenario, Severity, Verification Strategy.
19	5. **Sibling sweep, not single hit**: When a confirmed defect is one instance of a structurally repeated pattern (same algorithm reimplemented per ecosystem/mode/branch), grep for every other instance before reporting it as one finding. List all sibling locations in the same finding and note whether the fix should be "patch each copy" or "unify into one implementation" — the latter is preferred whenever N>1 copies exist. A finding that names only the first instance you tripped over, when siblings exist, is an incomplete finding.

16

20

23	- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.

27	
28	## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies
29	
30	1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
31	2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
32	3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
33	4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
34	5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
35	6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.

40	
41	1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
42	2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
43	3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
44	4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
45	5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.

Callisto Architecture

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging version --emit-decision writes the decision file after successful apply release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm ``` Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Depth: - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits. - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. ## Extension seams Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. ## Current boundaries and planned changes `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations do not establish a complete Python file set or identical package bytes. Remaining v1 work is in [`docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`](docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). The canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); only the parts it marks as design are not implemented, and none is an extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. ## Not covered here - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md). # 2. The committed version decision is the release authority Status: Accepted (implemented in #54) ## Context - After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54). - Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`). ## Decision `callisto version --emit-decision ` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to ``. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision ` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate"). ## Options considered - **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. "Rather than teach the re-derivation about groups -- a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution -- this trusts the decision `callisto version` already computed and committed … One decision surface instead of two that can drift apart" (PR #54). ## Consequences - The released roster and versions are exactly those committed in the release PR. - The decision file is a wire contract. Its schema is versioned: `ReleaseDecisionV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 2, and the reader accepts 1 and 2 so an older release PR still plans (commit 7027bbfb0). - A decision whose entries do not match its own digest fails to decode (E166) before the diff cross-check. - PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution

# 9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated

Status: Accepted (implemented in #154)

## Context

- A rerun adopts effects that already landed (ADR 3), so it must decide whether an existing tag is the one it planned.
- The local check read the tag with `git for-each-ref` and compared the target commit and the annotation text. The remote check uses `git ls-remote`, which returns the tag object and peeled commit but not the annotation text, so it compared only the commit.
- The same repository state could therefore be adopted or rejected depending on whether the remote tag had been fetched.

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.
- **Keep the split (text locally, commit remotely)** — rejected: the outcome depends on fetch state.

## Consequences

- Local and remote checks agree.
- A tag with a different message is adopted. The receipt records only the peeled commit (`ProviderEvidenceV1::GitTag { peeled_commit }` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs`), and `gh release create --verify-tag` checks only that the tag exists.

## Enforcement

- Tests in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs` for local and remote observation (different annotation text is adopted; lightweight and other-commit tags conflict).
- REL-RERUN-02 and REL-RERUN-03 in `docs/specs/release.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something downstream starts reading the annotation text (release notes, signing policy, provenance).

## Sources

- Owner decision, `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- The fix in this PR: "fix: stop comparing tag annotation text in release rerun observation"
# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. The evidence is in `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- System findings and verification limits: `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.
# Release execution

The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI).
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. The operations form a DAG by prerequisite; `callisto_model::canonical_operation_order`, built on `michi-graph`, validates it (a cycle is reported as one operation on it) and fixes the order: the smallest topological order by operation id.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release/execution.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release build-python`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Managed release PR and workflow

Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.

- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.
- Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity.
- Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review.
- `version-pr` maintains the PR; `release` runs the local release route. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. The [action manifest](../../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml) defines current inputs and outputs.
- Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Plan and build jobs receive none. Temporary intent, receipt, artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, outside the checkout.

GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates source, provenance, plan, observations, transitions, terminality, receipts, and artifacts. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics. Recovery dispatch uses current orchestration on `main` with an explicit merged source SHA and runs credential-free `recovery-checks` instead of full `verify`.

The generated release action maps credentials without changing owner-defined publish hooks:

- npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point npm-compatible tools at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for native hooks and `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration.
- Bun: also set `NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN`, because Bun does not honor `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`.
- PyPI: map `PYPI_TOKEN` to `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` for upload. The build backend receives no registry or forge credentials.
- Cargo: pass `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` through to Cargo.

## Run envelope and state (`release/execution.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.
- An npm registry publish is the exception to "then confirmed": it is issued, stays `Attempting`, and another npm publish may follow it. When nothing else can start, the executor looks at all issued publishes together until each is shown or the longest `confirm-timeout` is spent. That window is one `ConfirmationWave`: it opens when the first publish is issued, is measured on the provider set's clock so looking counts, and a publish shown along the way does not restart it. Each look is given the window that is left as its patience, so a registry that asks for long waits between tries cannot hold a look past the window; a look that has none left tries once. The tag, release draft, uploads and publication wait for the confirmation, so nothing is announced before the registry shows the version. Cargo and PyPI publishes are confirmed as they are published (PyPI completion is a file set, not a version).

Provider reads use native tools for Cargo and npm, and `curl` for PyPI's PEP 691 JSON simple index:

- Cargo: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY` runs from the source root. Matching `version:` means exact; exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent. Other results are indeterminate. Yanked versions are invisible to `cargo info`; a rejected publish ends without a receipt.
- npm: `npm view NAME@VERSION --json --fetch-retries=0`.
- PyPI: a matching file means exact; 404 or no match means absent; transport failure or non-JSON means indeterminate. Yanked matches count as absent. Before an effect, `release execute` also builds the release's files once into a temporary directory and compares their names with the index, so a partly uploaded release uploads only what is missing and is satisfied only when the whole set is there.

Adopting a version that is already published is by design, so a rerun can finish a half-done release. Because a foreign package would be adopted the same way, a Cargo or npm adoption also reads the repository the registry records for that version (`repository:` in `cargo info`, `repository` in `npm view`) and warns, without blocking, when it names a different repository from `origin`. A registry that records none, or a failed read, says nothing; PyPI's simple index records no repository, so it is not checked.

These reads are version-level checks, not proof of identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. Registry endpoints must be HTTPS. Read-only observations before an effect retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines.

After a registry publish the version may not be readable yet: npm serves a package's document with `max-age=300`, a missing package's 404 included, so a read just before the publish can answer stale for five minutes. The confirmation therefore waits by time, not tries, treating absent and unreachable as lag until the registry's window (`confirm-timeout`, default 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo) is spent, then fails with E157. An exact version or a conflict ends the wait at once.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
- GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`).

The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. An intent derived before either rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.

## Wire and observation boundaries

Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. The CLI's `release-pr verify` reader accepts both the strict bare decision and unchanged decide report, validating the report metadata before passing the payload to the shared domain constructor. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs.

Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect.

Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-i

# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state

Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)

## Context

- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).

## Decision

Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).

## Options considered

- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).

## Consequences

- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
- A registry publish that is complete once its version is visible (npm) is issued and confirmed in two steps within one run: the executor issues every publish it can, lets another npm publish follow an issued one, and confirms the issued publishes together before anything is announced. The issued set lives in memory like the rest of the run; a crash between issue and confirmation leaves the operation unproven, and the rerun observes it first, as for any other effect.
- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index, not when the version is visible (E306, E307).

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.

## Revisit when

- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".

## Sources

- PR #124 (592396564), commit bodies and PR body; closed PR #122
- PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution
- Incident report §2, §6 (F-003), §8 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)

Adopting a version that is already published is by design, so a rerun can finish a half-done release. Because a foreign package would be adopted the same way, a Cargo or npm adoption also reads the repository the registry records for that version (`repository:` in `cargo info`, `repository` in `npm view`) and warns, without blocking, when it names a different repository from `origin`. Read-only observations before an effect retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines.

After a registry publish the version may not be readable yet: npm serves a package's document with `max-age=300`, a missing package's 404 included, so a read just before the publish can answer stale for five minutes. ## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
- GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`).

The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs.

Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. `setup-callisto` defaults to `source: auto`: install the requested release, even in a Callisto checkout. An explicit `version` wins; otherwise `latest` resolves the pinned action ref to its `callisto@` release when possible. A `callisto-cli` manifest alone does not select checkout source.

GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. # 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state

Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)

## Context

- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).

## Decision

Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).

## Options considered

- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).

## Consequences

- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
- A registry publish that is complete once its version is visible (npm) is issued and confirmed in two steps within one run: the executor issues every publish it can, lets another npm publish follow an issued one, and confirms the issued publishes together before anything is announced. The issued set lives in memory like the rest of the run; a crash between issue and confirmation leaves the operation unproven, and the rerun observes it first, as for any other effect.
- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index, not when the version is visible (E306, E307).

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.

## Revisit when

- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".

## Sources

- PR #124 (592396564), commit bodies and PR body; closed PR #122
- PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution
- Incident report §2, §6 (F-003), §8 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
# 9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated

Status: Accepted (implemented in #154)

## Context

- A rerun adopts effects that already landed (ADR 3), so it must decide whether an existing tag is the one it planned.
- The local check read the tag with `git for-each-ref` and compared the target commit and the annotation text. The remote check uses `git ls-remote`, which returns the tag object and peeled commit but not the annotation text, so it compared only the commit.
- The same repository state could therefore be adopted or rejected depending on whether the remote tag had been fetched.

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.
- **Keep the split (text locally, commit remotely)** — rejected: the outcome depends on fetch state.

## Consequences

- Local and remote checks agree.
- A tag with a different message is adopted. The receipt records only the peeled commit (`ProviderEvidenceV1::GitTag { peeled_commit }` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs`), and `gh release create --verify-tag` checks only that the tag exists.

## Enforcement

- Tests in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs` for local and remote observation (different annotation text is adopted; lightweight and other-commit tags conflict).
- REL-RERUN-02 and REL-RERUN-03 in `docs/specs/release.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something downstream starts reading the annotation text (release notes, signing policy, provenance).

## Sources

- Owner decision, `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- The fix in this PR: "fix: stop comparing tag annotation text in release rerun observation"

The confirmation therefore waits by time, not tries, treating absent and unreachable as lag until the registry's window (`confirm-timeout`, default 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo) is spent, then fails with E157. An exact version or a conflict ends the wait at once.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
- GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`).

The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. An intent derived before either rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.

## Wire and observation boundaries

Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. The CLI's `release-pr verify` reader accepts both the strict bare decision and unchanged decide report, validating the report metadata before passing the payload to the shared domain constructor. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs.

Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect.

Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. With a sealed set, a build job (`release build-python`, no credentials) builds the files and `release artifact-manifest --seal-python` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the envelope's manifest digest covers them. `release execute` verifies the bytes, builds nothing, uploads those files, and treats any index file under a sealed name with another sha256 as an error (E307). The sealed sets are all or none per plan and each belongs to a Python publish of the intent; the manifest stays at schema version 1 because a manifest without sets is unchanged and an older reader rejects the new field. Artifact size/sha256 validation otherwise applies to declared GitHub assets. A PyPI registry reads its simple index at `url` and uploads to `publish-url` when set, else `url`; both endpoints are part of the registry binding. Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes are not supported.

## Verification tiers

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.

## Installer and product assets

`setup-callisto` defaults to `source: auto`: install the requested release, even in a Callisto checkout. An explicit `version` wins; otherwise `latest` resolves the pinned action ref to its `callisto@` release when possible. A `callisto-cli` manifest alone does not select checkout source.

`source: local` builds the checkout and ignores `version`. It requires tracked root and CLI manifests, the CLI entrypoint, a Cargo-confirmed workspace member and binary target, Git, Cargo, jq, and locked offline metadata resolution. It uses the checkout's `target/` cache, installs under `RUNNER_TEMP`, and never falls back from invalid local source. Callisto's release jobs use this mode.

Downloaded binaries are checked with `gh attestation verify` against `orin-dx/callisto` and the `callisto-release.yml` signer before extraction. Only the `callisto` binary is extracted. `verification: require` aborts on failure; `fallback` (default) deletes the asset and installs from crates.io; `skip` warns and uses it. Fallback pins the requested version except for `latest`. Older unattested releases motivate the default. `require` and `fallback` never run an unverified asset.

Product assets target `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. The Intel macOS asset is cross-compiled on an Apple silicon runner, and the arm64 Linux asset is built natively on an arm64 runner. Apple signing and notarization are out of scope. GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. Callisto publishes its crates to crates.io and product assets to GitHub Releases, not to another registry for rehearsal.
